title: Addition stories
examples: Teacher, how do I show this with numbers?
Can you show me another story problem?

explain.say: Listen to a story. You have two apples. Then you get three more apples. How many apples do you have now?
Count them all. One, two, three, four, five. So two and three make five.
You can also count on from the bigger number. Start at three. Count on two more: four, five.
You can write the story as a number sentence. Two plus three equals five.
Plus means put together. Equals means the same amount as.

faq.a: It means putting groups together to find a total amount. You are joining two separate amounts into one group.
asks: How do I put things together?

faq.q: Is counting on the same as adding?
faq.a: Yes, counting on is a quick way to add numbers. You start at one number and count up by the other number.
asks: Can I count on for addition?
Is counting on a math trick?

faq.q: Why do I write a number sentence?
faq.a: A number sentence writes the story in numbers and signs. It uses signs like plus and equals.
asks: How do I write the problem?

faq.q: What if the story has three groups?
faq.a: You can keep adding them one by one. You can write it like two plus three plus one equals six.
asks: Can I add more than two numbers?
What if there are three groups?

faq.q: Do I always need to use plus when combining?
faq.a: Yes, when you are putting things together, you use the plus sign. It means you are joining the groups.
asks: What sign do I use for joining?
Should I use plus or minus?

facts: Addition means putting groups together to find a total.
You can use your fingers to help you count when adding.
The plus sign means you are combining amounts.
An equals sign shows the total answer to the problem.

quiz.say: Count all the cars. Tap how many altogether.
quiz.why: Three cars and two cars make five cars.

wrong.0: One car was counted twice, so touch each car once.
wrong.1: Three is just the red cars, so count the blue cars too.

quiz.say: Start at 4. Count on 3 more. Tap the answer.
quiz.why: Start at four and count on three: five, six, seven.

wrong.0: Start counting on from the next number, which is five.
wrong.2: Four is where you start, so count on three more.

quiz.say: Three balloons. Five more balloons join them. Tap the number sentence.

options.say: five take away three equals two

quiz.why: Joining means adding. Three and five make eight.

wrong.1: Take away is for when some leave, and here more balloons join.
wrong.2: Count all the balloons again, because there are eight.
